gaps.sentence: His ___ (BEHAVE) at school has improved enormously.
Be careful not to ___ the medicine — read the label twice (USE).
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misuse means to use something incorrectly. A base verb follows 'not to'.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (ARRIVE) of the train was announced.
gaps.explanation: The subject must be a noun: arrival (-al noun of 'arrive').

gaps.sentence: She showed great ___ (PATIENT) with the children.
gaps.hint: noun needed; beware the similar word meaning 'people in hospital'
gaps.explanation: 'Patience' is the noun (show patience); 'patients' are people receiving medical care.

gaps.sentence: Club ___ (MEMBER) costs fifty euros a year.
gaps.explanation: "Membership costs" — the fee noun, not the person.

gaps.sentence: She was fired for ___ behaviour at work (PROFESSIONAL).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed before the noun 'behaviour'
gaps.explanation: The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unprofessional behaviour is behaviour below professional standards.

gaps.sentence: He had a happy ___ in the countryside (CHILD).
gaps.hint: noun needed: the period of being a child (-hood)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -hood forms period-of-life nouns: childhood.

gaps.sentence: The treaty will strengthen economic ___ between the two countries (COOPERATE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is followed by a noun: cooperation (-tion noun).
